newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas use up 13.4 pct, coal off 10.8 pct in Q3.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas use up 13.4 pct, coal off 10.8 pct in Q3.

text.p: Britain's total inland fuel consumption rose by 1.5 percent in the third quarter of this year compared to the same period a year ago, the Department of Trade and Industry said in a statement on Tuesday.

Total consumption -- which includes fuel delivered into storage as well as fuel used in the period -- rose to 45.7 million tonnes of oil equivalent in the period. By far the biggest increase was for natural gas, which rose by 13.4 percent compared to the corresponding period in the previous year. The DTI says this is "largely due to a significant increase in use for electricity generation".
Petroleum consumption was up by 3.6 percent. Petroleum use, including non-energy use, rose by 3.1 percent to 21.0 million tonnes in the third quarter.
But coal consumption continues to fall. Consumption in the third quarter was off by 10.8 percent in comparison with the same period last year.
